## Owner-word wake: no routine counts as set up without its GitHub trigger

In an adopting app, the setup session created the owner-word wake task through a tool that supports only a cron
schedule or a one-shot run. The task had no schedule and no GitHub trigger, the session reported it as set up, and
`autonomy.ownerWordWake` said `"routine"`. Owner-word issues then sat untouched (#91).

- **`routines/owner-word-wake.md`, setup brief.** Says plainly that a GitHub event trigger can be added only in the
  routines web UI (claude.ai/code/routines) or with a tool that explicitly supports it. A session that cannot add it
  creates nothing, or creates the task and gives the owner the exact UI steps and the task link, and never reports
  the routine as working. The brief now verifies the trigger (the task shows it, or the owner confirms it) before
  `autonomy.ownerWordWake` becomes `"routine"`; until then the value is `"none"`. New section "Testing it".
- **`routines/README.md`:** how to test the routine (open one `owner-word` issue and look for the routine's run).
- **Installer notice and doctor note** follow the same order: `"routine"` only after the trigger is verified. The
  doctor note `owner-word-wake-undeclared` stays.
- **Release gate:** `validate.mjs` fails when the setup brief drops any of these rules or the README drops the test.

Adopting apps that declared `"routine"`: open the task in claude.ai/code/routines and check that it shows a GitHub
trigger on issues (opened, labeled). If it does not, add the trigger there, or set `autonomy.ownerWordWake` to
`"none"` until it does. Then open one `owner-word` issue and check that the routine runs.
